Looking at the demo: the grid is divided into bands by the full rows/columns of 3s, and each scattered cell is replicated into every band at the same relative (offset) position.

Test: lines at rows 6 and 13 (three row-bands of 6), no column lines, so bottom-band pattern copies to top and middle bands.

```python
def transform(grid):
    H, W = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    cnt = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    bg = cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # find line rows / cols: fully uniform rows whose color != bg
    line_rows = [r for r in range(H) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1 and grid[r][0] != bg]
    line_cols = [c for c in range(W) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(H)}) == 1 and grid[0][c] != bg]
    line_color = grid[line_rows[0]][0] if line_rows else (grid[0][line_cols[0]] if line_cols else None)

    def bands(sizes_total, line_idx, size):
        bs, start = [], 0
        for l in line_idx:
            if l > start: bs.append((start, l - start))
            start = l + 1
        if start < size: bs.append((start, size - start))
        return bs

    rb = bands(H, line_rows, H)
    cb = bands(W, line_cols, W)

    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    def rband(r):
        for i,(s,h) in enumerate(rb):
            if s <= r < s+h: return i, r-s
        return None
    def cband(c):
        for j,(s,w) in enumerate(cb):
            if s <= c < s+w: return j, c-s
        return None

    cells = [(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(H) for c in range(W)
             if grid[r][c] != bg and grid[r][c] != line_color]
    for r,c,v in cells:
        ri = rband(r); cj = cband(c)
        if ri is None or cj is None: continue
        i, orr = ri; j, occ = cj
        for i2,(s2,h2) in enumerate(rb):
            if orr >= h2: continue
            for j2,(s3,w3) in enumerate(cb):
                if occ >= w3: continue
                tr, tc = s2+orr, s3+occ
                if out[tr][tc] == bg:
                    out[tr][tc] = v
    return out
```

This reproduces the demo (checked mentally: copies of 7 at (5,3) and 6 at (7,4) into all four quadrant offsets) and tiles the bottom band of the test into the top and middle bands.
